content: 1. Fedratinib and Pentamidine: Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of pentamidine by altering CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Conversely, pentamidine increases the levels or effects of fedratinib. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs considered, as the interaction with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors has not been studied. 2. Fexinidazole and Pentamidine: Fexinidazole increases pentamidine levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval, necessitating avoidance or alternative therapy. Co-administration with potassium channel blockers or QT-prolonging drugs should be avoided. 3. Pentamidine and Finerenone: Pentamidine increases finerenone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required, particularly for serum potassium during dose adjustments. 4. Fingolimod and Pentamidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs are recommended. 5. Flecainide and Pentamidine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 6. Flibanserin and Pentamidine: Pentamidine increases flibanserin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the risk of increased adverse effects. 7. Fluconazole and Pentamidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Fluoxetine and Pentamidine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 9. Fluphenazine and Pentamidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Fluvoxamine and Pentamidine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 11. Pentamidine and Folic Acid: Pentamidine decreases folic acid levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents and is of minor or unknown significance. 12. Formoterol and Pentamidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 13. Foscarnet and Pentamidine: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Close monitoring is required due to the risk of severe hypocalcemia. 14. Fostemsavir and Pentamidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised, especially at higher doses of fostemsavir. 15. Gadobenate and Pentamidine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 16. Ganciclovir and Pentamidine: Ganciclovir increases pentamidine toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 17. Gemifloxacin and Pentamidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 18. Gemtuzumab and Pentamidine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 19. Gentamicin and Pentamidine: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 20. Gepirone and Pentamidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 21. Gilteritinib and Pentamidine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 22. Givosostat and Pentamidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. If co-administration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at baseline and during treatment. Withhold therapy if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or increases by more than 60 ms from baseline. 23. Glasdegib and Pentamidine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, monitor for QTc prolongation. 24. Glucarpidase and Pentamidine: Glucarpidase decreases pentamidine levels by increasing metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 25. Goserelin and Pentamidine: Goserelin increases pentamidine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the risk of torsades de pointes. 26. Granisetron and Pentamidine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 27. Haloperidol and Pentamidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Histrelin and Pentamidine: Histrelin increases pentamidine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the risk of torsades de pointes. 31. Ibutilide and Pentamidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 32. Ifosfamide and Pentamidine: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. Caution and monitoring of renal function are required. 33. Iloperidone and Pentamidine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 34. Imipramine and Pentamidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 35. Indacaterol and Pentamidine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 36. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, monitor ECGs and electrolytes before and during treatment. 38. Insulin and Pentamidine: Pentamidine may cause hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, followed by the opposite effect. Insulin dosage adjustments and increased glucose monitoring may be required. 39. Ioversol and Pentamidine: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 40.
